source.title: PNT-Edge: Towards Robust Edge Detection with Noisy Labels by Learning Pixel-level Noise Transitions
source.authors: Wen-Jie Xuan; Shanshan Zhao; Yu Yao; Ju-Hua Liu; Tong-Liang Liu; Yixin Chen; Bo Du; Da-Cheng Tao

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether an edge detector learns clean labels before memorizing noisy labels, using noisy-versus-clean evaluation over training rather than the original classification setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training dynamics for noisy edge labels. It does not test completely random labelings, unstructured inputs, or controlled fractions of corrupted labels. Cited results from Arpit et al. and ADELE are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: Section 4.4 reports the study's own training dynamics in a new setting, semantic edge detection. Comparing clean and noisy annotations over training bears directly on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: Section 4.4 interprets the dynamics as learning clean edges before memorizing noisy annotations. The paper's overall conclusion is that PNT-Edge reduces the impact of annotation noise and produces more precise edge maps.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CASENet-S on noisy semantic edge annotations and compares training-time metrics on noisy and clean labels; it does not reproduce the random-label experiments.
record.problems: The training-dynamics result is described in text but its values are presented in Figure 5; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The experiment uses noisy edge annotations rather than random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No additional findings on the claim versions were reported by this study. Other tables evaluate the proposed method's edge-detection performance rather than random-label fitting or the clean-before-noisy learning dynamic.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across controlled corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Completely random labels and direct comparison of learning dynamics between separately trained real-label and random-label models.

record.verdict_notes: The noise consists of naturally misaligned edge annotations, rather than random class assignments. The paired metric trajectories support V6 qualitatively; they do not establish perfect memorization or quantify uncertainty. Other performance and ablation tables are already declared outside the record's scope and do not supply additional tests of these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, chance test error, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost of fitting random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Controlled corruption fractions from none to all, training-set fit, and test-error trajectory.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation change fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
The study tests noisy edge annotations, not random labels, and does not compare distinct learning mechanisms for real and random labels.

rows.subject: CASENet-S
rows.operation_detail: Train on noisy edge labels and evaluate metrics on noisy labels over training.

conditions.value: SBD re-annotated test set; 847/212 images for train/test

rows.measure: Training-set metrics on noisy labels over epochs
rows.value: Metrics on noisy labels keep increasing; rapid increment of ODS-F and mAP at about 20 epochs.
rows.note: The text reports the trend without giving the plotted metric values.
rows.check: The reported trend is accurate. Its evidence for V6 depends on comparison with R2; increasing noisy-label metrics alone would not establish the learning order. No numerical curve values are available in the supplied text.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.4, Figure 5 discussion, lines 1165–1182; backbone in Section 4.5, lines 1189–1191.

rows.subject: CASENet-S
rows.operation_detail: Train on noisy edge labels and evaluate metrics on clean labels over training.

conditions.value: SBD re-annotated test set; 847/212 images for train/test

rows.measure: Training-set metrics on clean labels over epochs
rows.value: Metrics on clean labels only increase at early stages, then are saturated.
rows.note: The authors say this verifies that detectors first fit clean labels and then memorize noisy labels; plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The reported trend is accurate. Clarify that clean labels are evaluation targets for the model trained with noisy labels, not a separate clean-label training condition. Interpret jointly with R1.

relationships.condition: CASENet-S trained on noisy semantic edge annotations using the 847-image training split of the re-annotated SBD subset.
relationships.reason: Clean-label metrics improve early and saturate while noisy-label metrics continue improving, with a rapid increase around epoch 20; this supports clean-before-noisy learning in this setting (R1, R2).
relationships.display_finding: Clean-label metrics improved early and saturated, while noisy-label metrics continued improving with a rapid increase around epoch 20.
